title: Churros with Chocolate–Dulce de Leche Dip
summary: Crisp ridged churros served with a thick, glossy dip of dark chocolate and dulce de leche.
equipment: stand mixer with paddle (or hand mixer)
piping bag with a 1.5 cm closed star nozzle
baking tray lined with oiled baking paper
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Bring the water, butter, sugar and salt to the boil in the large saucepan. Take it off the heat, tip in all the flour and beat until it comes together in a smooth ball.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Move the dough to the mixer bowl and beat on low for 1 min to let off steam. Add the eggs and vanilla in two goes and beat on medium until the dough is smooth, thick and shiny.

steps.title: Pipe
steps.text: Spoon the dough into the piping bag and pipe 18 lengths of 14 cm onto the oiled paper, cutting each with scissors. Chill them uncovered for 15-30 min so the ridges stay sharp.

steps.title: Make the dip
steps.text: Warm the milk in the small pan until it steams, take it off the heat and add the chocolate and cocoa. After 2 min whisk until smooth, then whisk in the dulce de leche until thick and glossy. Keep it warm over the lowest heat.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Fill the pan with oil to about 4 cm, no more than half full, and heat it to 190 °C.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Fry 5-6 churros at a time for 5-6 min, turning now and then, keeping the oil at 180-190 °C, until deep golden and crisp. Snap one open to check it is cooked through and not pasty, then drain on the rack.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the churros hot, 3 per person, with the warm dip.

tips: The most common mistake is frying in oil that is not hot enough; below 180 °C the churros soak up oil and turn soggy.
Chilling the piped dough keeps the ridges crisp and stops it splitting.
Stir a splash of hot milk into the dip if it thickens on standing.
Use a closed star nozzle; open ones give flat ridges that burn.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Churros are best straight from the pan. The dip keeps covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; warm gently before serving.
